2. The petitioners instituted the aforesaid suit stating, inter alia, that two full brothers Shaikh Kazim and Shaikh Nazim were the owners in equal share of the land mentioned in the schedule to the plaint of the suit, Shaikh Kazim died leaving a son Kayesuddin and a daughter Rabdan Nessa, who died subsequently leaving the plaintiffs as her heirs. Shaikh Nazim died leaving three sons, namely Eman Baksh, Rahim Baksh and Jahiruddin and three daughters, namely Amela Bibi, Begum Bibi and Taimun . Nessa. Eman Baksh, father of defendant Nos. 1-6, aforesaid Jahiruddin and Rahim Baksh (who were opposite party No. 7 and B before the High Court Division) inherited .11 acres of land from their father Shaikh Nazim. They on 11.10.64 proposed to sell .06th acres of land to the plaintiff-petitioners at a consideration of Tk. 1000/- and on receipt of Tk. 200/- executed are unregistered bainapatra in their favour and also delivered possession of the land to them. C 1.10.67 they further made an oral agreement to sell further .04 acres of land to the plaintiffs at a consideration of Tk. 2000/- and on receipt of Tk. 1000/- also handed over possession of the said land to the plaintiffs on 12.17. 68. Thereafter those sellers had left the locality and started leaving in another Union. Later t said Eman Baksh, Rahim Baksh and Jahiruddin did not execute the relevant kabalas. The plaintiffs thus, claimed title to the aforesaid property of 11 acres out of Plot No. 1001 of C.S. Khatian No. 494 by way of adverse possession. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 4-11 and 14 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the claim of the plaintiffs. Their case is. Keyasuddin son of Shaikh-Kazim died childless leaving behind Jamal Baksh, Baksh, Amal Baksh, Rahim Baksh, Jahiruddin Baksh, Eman Baksh. Amela Begum, Begum Bibi and Taimurnessa as his heirs. S. A. Khatian Nos. 398, 399 have been prepared in the names of the heirs of both Shaikh Kazim and Shaikh Nazim and accordingly they have been possessing the same. The plaintiffs got only 8 decimals out of total 19 decimals land of Plot No. 1001 and they sold out their entire 8 decimals share to Rafijuddin the father of defendant No. 14. They also denied the execution of bainapatra or of making oral agreement in respect of the disputed land by Eman Baksh, Rahim Baksh and Jahiruddin. They denied the plaintiffs' possession right, title and interest in the suit land.
